course.title: Database Management System: Organizing, Querying, and Managing Data
course.type: Professional Core and Professional Elective Courses
course.rationale: This course provides a comprehensive introduction to Database Management Systems (DBMS), with a focus on Oracle SQL and PL/SQL. It covers data, information, database structures, DBMS architecture and components, SQL basics and advanced queries, normalization, transaction management, data integrity through constraints, PL/SQL programming, stored procedures, triggers, user management and security. Learners develop database design, implementation and administration skills using Oracle/MySQL tools.

executionProfile.explicitSecondaryEnvironment: MySQL Workbench is specifically named for the Module 5 Interactive Trigger Simulation evaluation activity.
executionProfile.implementationNote: Oracle SQL/PLSQL practicals must not be reported as successfully executed by a SQLite/MySQL/Judge0 SQL substitute. Use a configured, isolated Oracle-compatible lab service for execution and database-state checking; without it, the portal reports only preflight/syntax status and does not mark a practical complete. The separate MySQL Workbench trigger activity is labeled as such.

courseOutcomes.text: Understand foundational database concepts and Oracle SQL syntax to design, query, and manage relational databases effectively.
Explore Oracle database architecture and implement data integrity through constraints, functions, and best practices in database design.
Develop advanced SQL querying skills and apply normalization, transaction control, and database design principles for efficient and reliable data management.
Apply PL/SQL programming constructs, including cursors and exception handling, to develop secure and efficient database applications.
Implement advanced database features using stored procedures, triggers, transaction control, user management, and Oracle security privileges for effective database administration.

instructionalMethod: Course delivery depends on content requirements and student needs; in addition to conventional blackboard teaching, instructors may use demonstrations, role play, quizzes, brainstorming, MOOCs and similar tools.
Ten percent of the content topics are suggested for flipped-mode instruction.
Supplementary resources may include online videos, NPTEL/SWAYAM videos, e-courses and a Virtual Laboratory.
Internal evaluation is based on the Active Learning Assignment.
A practical/viva examination is conducted at semester end to evaluate laboratory performance.
referenceBooks: Database System Concepts, 6th Edition — Abraham Silberschatz, Henry F. Korth and S. Sudarshan, McGraw-Hill.
Oracle 8i — Jase A. Ramalho, BPB Publication.
An Introduction to Database Systems — C. J. Date, Pearson.
Database Management System — Ramakrishnan and Gehrke, Tata McGraw-Hill.
sourceNotes: All five modules, topic labels, ordering, hours, weightages, practical prompts, assessment activities and course outcomes are transcribed from the attached 12-page scanned syllabus.
The PDF's Module 1 Practical 12 wording is internally inconsistent (it says DDL and then 'Create minimum 10 records'). The manifest preserves the scan's wording and does not reinterpret it.

The syllabus provides practical prompts but no per-topic quiz question bank. Any optional portal practice questions are labeled as generated learning checks based only on syllabus topics, not as official questions.
The syllabus rationale emphasizes Oracle SQL/PLSQL, while the Module 5 trigger simulation assessment explicitly names MySQL Workbench. Those environments are kept distinct.

modules.title: Introduction to Database Management Concept and SQL Basics

topics.title: Data Definition Language (DDL): CREATE, ALTER, DROP
Data Manipulation Language (DML): INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE
Oracle Data Dictionary: USER_TABLES and ALL_TABLES

practicals.prompt: Implement SQL queries for Creating and describing tables (CREATE, DESC).
Implement SQL queries for Modifying tables using ALTER.
Implement SQL queries for Deleting tables using DROP.
Implement SQL queries for creating tables and insert sample data in tables.
Implement SQL queries for Inserting and updating records using INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE.
Implement SQL queries for Retrieving data using SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY.
Implement SQL queries using aggregate functions with GROUP BY and HAVING.
Create Two tables' Students and Employees with 5 fields and stored actual data into the table using create and insert command.
Create student tables with a few columns representing common data types (integer, text, date etc.) using DDL commands.
Implement SQL Queries to perform DDL Commands (Create 5 tables and perform all the DDL operations upon them).
Insert sample data into your tables using SQL INSERT statements. Verify the data has been inserted correctly.
Implement SQL Queries to perform DDL Commands (Create minimum 10 records and perform modification operations upon them).
Practice DDL-create and DML-insert commands.
Retrieve data using the SELECT command from table.
Practice using SQL UPDATE and DELETE statements to modify data.
Implement SQL queries for Understanding and browsing data dictionary USER_TABLES, ALL_TABLES.

assessments.title: Scenario-Based Case Simulation
assessments.description: A clinic database storing doctor and patient information. Design tables (DDL), populate them (DML), write queries using WHERE and GROUP BY to answer case questions (including patient counts per doctor and doctors treating more than three patients), and retrieve metadata such as USER_TABLES.

assessments.title: DBMS Vocabulary Crossword
assessments.description: Complete an individually provided DBMS-concepts crossword and upload the solved copy to the GMIU portal.

modules.title: Database System Architecture and Ensuring Data Integrity

practicals.prompt: Apply primary keys and Not NULL constraints.
Implementing NOT NULL, CHECK, UNIQUE.
Using IN operator in queries.
Perform queries involving predicates LIKE, BETWEEN, IN etc.
Practice with numeric, date, and string inbuilt functions.
Add constraints like Primary key, NOT NULL and UNIQUE to your tables.
Use foreign keys to establish relationships between tables.
Implement practical 1 again with referential constraint.
Implement SQL queries using Date functions like add-months, months-between, round, next day, truncate, etc.
Implement SQL queries using Numeric functions like abs, ceil, power, mod, round, trunc, sqrt, etc.
Implement SQL queries and String Functions like initcap, lower, upper, rtrim, replace, substring, instr, etc.
Implement SQL queries using Conversion functions like to-char, to-date, to-number.
Implement SQL queries using Group functions like Avg, Min, Max, Sum, Count, etc.

assessments.title: Design and Justify Challenge
assessments.description: Build a student management system, select at least three constraints, and justify where and why each applies, including possible consequences if it is not applied.

assessments.title: Design Your Own Mini-Database
assessments.description: Choose a real-world scenario; design at least three entities and their table names, fields, types and constraints; identify primary/foreign-key relationships; add at least five sample records per table; write SELECT, WHERE, join and aggregate queries; prepare the specified report.

practicals.prompt: To understand and implement various types of SQL joins — inner join, outer join (left, right, full), and self join.

To learn how to retrieve and display combined data from multiple relational database tables using different types of SQL joins, thereby understanding data relationships and improving data querying efficiency.

To practice the use of different types of subqueries — multiple-row, nested, and correlated — in SQL, enabling complex data extraction from multiple related tables based on dynamic or dependent conditions.
To develop the skill to solve complex SQL queries using subqueries, including single-row and multiple-row subqueries, thereby enhancing query logic and data manipulation capabilities.

To explore the usage of conditional operators EXISTS, ANY, and ALL in SQL for querying datasets with conditions involving comparisons against subquery results, supporting advanced decision-making in data retrieval.

To understand and implement set operators — UNION, INTERSECT, and MINUS — for combining the results of multiple SQL queries and refining output by eliminating duplicates or performing comparisons between datasets.

To demonstrate the creation and practical usage of database objects such as views (for virtual tables), indexes (for query performance optimization), and sequences (for auto-generating unique values), enhancing database design and efficiency.
Demonstrating Transactions: COMMIT, ROLLBACK, SAVEPOINT.

To perform database backup and recovery operations using export and import utilities, ensuring data protection and availability by understanding the process of safeguarding data in case of failure or loss.

assessments.title: Operation Data Phoenix: Rebuild & Secure the Crashed System
assessments.description: Rebuild a crashed hospital database from a partial backup, address an unnormalized schema and integrity issues related to unauthorized access, reconstruct the schema, query evidence with advanced SQL, use views/indexes/synonyms, simulate transactions, verify serializability, and prepare a backup/recovery plan. Submit the report.

assessments.title: Design a Mini Social Media Platform Database
assessments.description: Individually design a mini social-media database, create tables, insert sample data, and write queries for posts, likes, comments and followers.

practicals.prompt: Implement basic PL/SQL blocks.
Implement PL/SQL programs using IF STATEMENT.
Implement PL/SQL programs using WHILE LOOP.
Implement PL/SQL programs using IF, CASE, and loops.
Implement PL/SQL programs with Cursor implementation (all types).
Implement PL/SQL programs using Exception handling examples.

assessments.title: Mini Project Sprint
assessments.description: Work on a real-world project (for example, a college enrollment system): design a normalized schema, write PL/SQL procedures, handle exceptions, implement security features, and demonstrate data recovery and transaction control.

assessments.title: DBMS Error Hunt
assessments.description: Individually identify and correct intentional mistakes in a faulty database design, PL/SQL block or SQL queries, including redundant data, missing relationships and incorrect SQL syntax or logic.

modules.title: Advanced Concepts of SQL & Access Control

topics.title: Roles: Create, Grant, View and Delete

practicals.prompt: Creating stored procedures and functions.
Creating and using packages.
Implement Cursor.
Implement Trigger.
Writing and testing triggers: BEFORE, AFTER, INSTEAD OF (Row/Statement-level).
Creating and managing users: CREATE and DELETE USER.
Using GRANT and REVOKE.
Demonstrating transaction control with SAVEPOINT and rollback.

assessments.title: Code Optimization
assessments.description: Optimize and refactor two suboptimal Oracle PL/SQL programs or scripts (for example, procedures, functions, packages or triggers) to improve readability, maintainability, security and performance without changing output or behavior.

assessments.title: Interactive Trigger Simulation Using MySQL Workbench
assessments.description: In MySQL Workbench, create a table and trigger, perform INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, observe automatic trigger execution, and document the trigger execution order. This named evaluation activity is kept distinct from the Oracle PL/SQL lab.
